problem: Which of the following is the graph of $y=-4{(\frac{1}{4})}^{x}-3?$
worked_solution:
To plot the given function, we follow these steps:

- We take the curve $y=4{(\frac{1}{4})}^{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932041/assets/c925aea9381d9ecb008b7ab609ef72817a7c8bc51a5e3ab5abf4fb33f9055730.png)

- Reflect it on the $x$-axis to give $y=-4{(\frac{1}{4})}^{x}.$ The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,4)$ to $(0,-4)$ but the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932041/assets/fa429123677e529f376c871642e0c4c0986cb5ea5319f7bf59b225ea0d36f792.png)

- Then, vertically shift it by $3$ units down to give $y=-4{(\frac{1}{4})}^{x}-3.$ The point $(0,-4)$ moves to $(0,-7)$ and the horizontal asymptote moves from $y=0$ to $y=-3.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932041/assets/3511221e88625a10cc41b1a1470c13c38ef9398afb88fa09ae2f033e88ad9696.png)
